Write a behaviour tree evaluator for game AI in pure Luau: nodes are plain tables and `tick(node, ctx, state)` returns `"success"`, `"failure"` or `"running"`. Node types: `{type = "action", fn = function(ctx) return status end}` (any other returned value raises an error), `{type = "condition", fn = ...}` (truthy -> success), `{type = "sequence", children = {...}}` (runs children in order, stops at the first failure or running), `{type = "selector", children}` (stops at the first success or running) and `{type = "inverter", child}` (swaps success and failure). An empty sequence succeeds, an empty selector fails, and an unknown type raises an error. Composites can also have `memory = true`: when a child returns running, the composite remembers its index in the `state` table (keyed by the node) and the next tick resumes from that child instead of starting over; the memory is cleared when the composite finishes. Without memory, every tick starts from the first child.

Write a text editor model in Luau with undo and redo: `Editor.new(text)`, `insert(pos, str)` (1-based position, `#text + 1` appends), `delete(pos, len)`, `undo()` and `redo()` (each returns false when there is nothing to do) and a `text` field.
